summary: Dell BIOS update enabled Thunderbolt user-authorization, preventing dock NIC init and blocking Autopilot provisioning
description:
Issue summary:
During automated Autopilot provisioning of newly imaged Dell Latitude fleet, devices attached to corporate Thunderbolt docks fail to bring the dock NIC up in OOBE. Autopilot times out and machines enter provisioning retry loop (OOBE restart). This started after we rolled BIOS package 1.7.3 on the deployment image branch (pushed 2026-03-09).

Impact:
- ~18 new hires' devices failed first-boot autopilot in us-west region (blocking satchel deliveries).
- Imaging throughput reduced; manual intervention required to complete onboarding for docked devices.

Environment:
- Windows 11 22H2 golden image (SCCM/Task Sequence), Autopilot profile provisioning, corp Thunderbolt docks (TB16 gen2), Dell BIOS 1.7.3, previous BIOS 1.6.8 was OK.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Apply SCCM task sequence with BIOS 1.7.3 to Latitude 7440 with TB16 dock attached.
2) Boot to Autopilot OOBE with ethernet via dock.
3) Observe OOBE network detection timeout and device restart (retries).

Observed behavior:
- Thunderbolt security mode changed from "No Security" to "User Authorization" after BIOS 1.7.3 update.
- Dock's NIC enumerates after user accepts thunderbolt device on-screen prompt; OOBE has already timed out by then.
- Event logs show network adapter not found during first-boot; Autopilot times out at ~8 minutes.

Expected behavior:
- Dock NIC should enumerate immediately during OOBE so Autopilot can complete without user interaction (same as prior BIOS 1.6.8).

Investigation notes:
- Confirmed reproducible on two lab units with TB16. Rollback to BIOS 1.6.8 restores previous behavior.
- BIOS release notes for 1.7.3 mention "Thunderbolt security enhancements" but do not call out default mode change.
- DellCommand Configure / WMI reports attribute: ThunderboltSecurityMode = 2 (User Authorization) on 1.7.3, previously 0 (No Security).
- SCCM BIOS package applied without extra vendor config; we expected BIOS vendor defaults to remain compatible with autopilot workflow.
- Network team confirmed Autopilot timeouts are normal when no NIC present during OOBE; typical workaround is user acceptance, but that is not possible during zero-touch onboarding.
- Reproduced in staging and prod images. Not related to cabling or switch config.

Temporary workaround applied:
- For incoming batches: temporarily gate BIOS 1.7.3 in SCCM and reimage affected units back to 1.6.8; this allowed Autopilot to complete without manual steps (applied to 18 devices so far).
- Developed a post-imaging SCCM step using DellCommand Configure (DCU) to set ThunderboltSecurityMode=0 prior to first boot. Applied to new task sequence in staging for immediate mitigation.

Root cause hypothesis:
- BIOS update 1.7.3 changes default Thunderbolt security to require user authorization; it prevents dock devices from being enumerated at pre-login stage, causing Autopilot OOBE to retry and fail.

Proposed remediation / long-term plan:
- Update golden image task sequence to include a DCU configuration step that forces Thunderbolt security to the legacy/no-security mode before first OOBE network check. (Short term, implemented as emergency change in staging.)
- Engage Dell support to request a BIOS option to preserve previous default or expose a persistent OEM setting we can configure silently during imaging. Opened SR 123456789.
- Add a preflight check in our imaging pipeline to detect BIOS-level security changes (scan DCU/BiosProvider attributes) and block image promotion if compatibility-impacting flags are changed.
- Communicate gating policy to site reliability and procurement: delay broad BIOS rollouts for new models until compatibility verification with Autopilot/docked scenarios is validated.

Resolution notes (work-in-progress):
- Workaround (DCU step) merged to staging TS (Task Sequence) 2026-03-11; initial run reimaged 6 units successfully.
- SCCM BIOS rollout paused for 1.7.3.
- Dell SR opened and vendor engineering has requested a BIOS dump; vendor estimate: 5 business days for root cause analysis.

Attachments / logs:
- Excerpt: System event log during OOBE: "NetworkAdapter: No adapters present at startup. Autopilot network detect timed out."
- DCU query output: ThunderboltSecurityMode=2 (on 1.7.3)
- Screenshot: OOBE thunderbolt pairing prompt (requires user acceptance).

Next steps:
- Continue reimaging remaining affected devices with rollback where necessary until DCU step validated across fleet.
- Track Dell SR and update when vendor provides remediation or a signed BIOS patch.
- Implement imaging pipeline preflight and update runbook for docking scenarios.
comments: Aisha Ramos (Support): Initial report from onboarding ops. Noticed spike in Autopilot failures for docked L7440 units after BIOS branch bump. Created ticket and paused further BIOS push.

Devon Patel (Imaging): Reproduced in lab. Confirmed TB security default flipped. Rolled back two units to 1.6.8 and Autopilot succeeded. Preparing DCU config to force setting to preserve zero-touch flow.
SRE - L. Nguyen: Suggest updating Autopilot network timeout as a stop-gap? Concerned that increasing timeout masks other failures and will slow onboarding. Prefer BIOS-level fix.
Procurement - R. Ellis: Flagging for hardware intake: we may need to request BIOS QA signoff from vendor for future firmware shipments for docked fleet.
Devon Patel: Applied DCU change in staging TS. Reimaged 6 devices attached to docks; all 6 completed Autopilot without manual intervention. Preparing change request to deploy DCU step to prod TS.
Aisha Ramos: Customer-facing note: Internal onboarding ops informed — manual acceptance required only if device shipped prior to workaround. New shipments will be imaged with DCU step.
Dell Support (SR 123456789): Acknowledged. Requested BIOS dump and two affected units for forensic. ETA 5 business days for initial analysis.
resolution: Workaround implemented: DCU configuration step to set ThunderboltSecurityMode=0 in task sequence and BIOS rollout paused. Vendor SR opened; long-term fix pending vendor response.
workaround: Reimage to BIOS 1.6.8 OR run DellCommand Configure step in SCCM task sequence to set ThunderboltSecurityMode=0 prior to first OOBE.
